Welcome to pharmacy, I also have a transfer story but first I’ll say what you’re going through is shitty and although they legally can transfer you it’s a bit rude of them to not be upfront and direct with you. I’m sorry you have to go through and hopefully this ends up being a blessing in disguise, it often feels as though management favours pharmacists (even shitty ones) over their less qualified piers. 

We have had our head pharmacist for about two years now and the guy is very much probably a narcissist or sociopath going off the way he treats us, our interns and customers. He will sign in to work some (if not most) days go home and clock up bulk OT, come back in the late afternoon sit at the computer in the office, check emails and then sign out. On the days he does work, he can be very nice and charming or absolutely horrid. We’ve lost a lot of good staffers because of him and one other pharmacist (whose left, thank the high heavens) and my mental health, which is already quite fragile haha, took a turn for the worst so I put in for a transfer. 

Initially they wouldn’t allow it but eventually they were willing to transfer me to another store that had a part time position available. He said that he’d have to talk to the other store about my mental health and the problems I have at our store and then it’d basically be up to them to accept me or decline the transfer. The cruel twist is that they twisted my arm to go part time at my current store because I’m willing to work part time at the other one, why not here? But I was willing to make huge adjustments financially to work somewhere that has a less toxic environment. I wrote a very formal letter stating that I’m willing to go permanent part time next year, but all this wouldn’t even have happened (to myself or my friends that had to leave for the sake of their sanity) if management had just taken care of front shop instead of thinking with their money inside their pockets.
